families.decision: Vanilla 26.1 sound_event is a client built-in registry, so reference holders use the generated static order while direct holders retain their inline location and fixed range.

Vanilla 26.1 synchronizes dialog definitions and uses Dialog.STREAM_CODEC only in ClientboundShowDialogPacket. The protocol preserves nonnegative session references or a bounded direct NBT compound and rejects invalid framing; world resolves server order and distinguishes valid, stub, malformed, and unknown entries, while direct and custom reordered referenced dialogs reach the complete native screen and nested-action lifecycle.

Vanilla 26.1 synchronizes ChatType.DIRECT_CODEC values and sends named or direct holders in player/disguised chat. Protocol retains the trusted Component payloads and direct decoration style; world resolves named holders only through the frozen session order, decodes chat/narration parameters and style, retains stub/malformed/unknown diagnostics, and preserves the no-server vanilla fallback. The native event test proves a custom entry inserted before minecraft:chat is not interpreted as the vanilla holder.

Vanilla 26.1 synchronizes JukeboxSong.DIRECT_CODEC values and uses named or direct holders in the jukebox_playable item component. Protocol retains direct-holder Component NBT; world resolves server holder order and decodes named/direct SoundEvent values, rich descriptions, positive length, and comparator output. Native audio and item tooltips consume the typed session value, including custom sound range and description, while data-less known-pack stubs alone may use resource-identity fallback and malformed or unknown entries never fall back by bootstrap ordinal.

Vanilla 26.1 synchronizes TrimMaterial.DIRECT_CODEC and TrimPattern.DIRECT_CODEC and sends named or direct holders in item components. Protocol retains direct Component NBT; world decodes synchronized assets, descriptions, overrides, and decal through current-session holder order with exact field diagnostics; renderer and tooltip consumers share that typed projection. Only known vanilla data-less stubs use resource-identity fallback, while custom stubs, malformed payloads, and unknown holders never fall back by bootstrap ordinal.

Vanilla 26.1 synchronizes BannerPattern.DIRECT_CODEC and sends named or direct holders in banner-pattern layers. Protocol retains both direct fields; world resolves current-session holder order with exact malformed-field diagnostics and only known vanilla data-less stubs use resource identity. Tooltip, persistent debug, block-entity projection, and banner_patterns atlas rendering consume the typed value; custom entries and reorder reach their own translation and sprite, while unknown holders never fall back by bootstrap ordinal.

Vanilla 26.1 synchronizes PaintingVariant.DIRECT_CODEC and sends named or inline holders in item components and painting entity metadata. Protocol retains both forms; world resolves the current-session holder order, stores named metadata identity with its exact resource/source/revision, validates width/height/asset/components, and permits resource-identity fallback only for known vanilla data-less stubs. Tooltips, entity bounds/direction, per-tile light, paintings-atlas sprites, and exact front/back/boundary geometry consume that typed projection; malformed and unknown entries never fall back by bootstrap ordinal.

Vanilla Instrument.STREAM_CODEC carries either a current-session holder id or all four DIRECT_STREAM_CODEC fields. Protocol retains the direct SoundEvent holder, exact float bits, styled description, and exact Component NBT; native persistence resolves named ids through the current session, reconstructs complete direct values, and fails closed for mixed or incomplete summaries.
The generated built-in holder catalogs preserve GameEvent field registration order and PoiTypes bootstrap order; canonical debug values replace holder ids with resource identity before publication.
This generic helper delegation is an implementation detail of holderSet; every concrete network holderSet factory call is covered by the network-holder-set-or-tag family.

The synchronized holder id selects the server entry order and is stored with exact resource/source/revision identity; the NETWORK_CODEC presentation is projected for all three families, and custom adult/baby textures become visible only after upload.

Vanilla 26.1 villager type and profession are client built-ins; entity VillagerData stores both generated resource identities with the frozen revision, while the villager-variant component uses the same generated fixed registry order. Configuration data cannot remap either path.

The synchronized unit-valued world-clock registry preserves server holder order; SetTime retains those holder ids, and the active dimension default resource id selects the matching session identity before clock merge and ticking.

Entity metadata holder ids resolve through each synchronized server registry and retain exact resource/source/revision identity; all five complete codec shapes project their required SoundEvent holders, and adult/baby hurt and death sounds reach positioned audio with custom order, direct range, stub, armor/bypass, malformed-payload, and stale-revision coverage.

The metadata holder id resolves through synchronized server order and retains exact resource/source/revision identity; CatVariant.NETWORK_CODEC projects both age-specific ResourceTexture assets, and entity rendering switches to the selected custom texture only after upload while stubs, stale revisions, and failures preserve the checked built-in fallback.

The metadata holder id resolves through synchronized server order and retains exact resource/source/revision identity; FrogVariant.NETWORK_CODEC projects its ResourceTexture, and the custom texture reaches the entity instance only after upload while stubs, stale revisions, and failures preserve the checked built-in identity fallback.

The metadata holder resolves through synchronized server order and retains exact resource/source/revision identity; ModelAndTexture projects the normal/warm model selector and ResourceTexture, and entity rendering switches both geometry and custom texture atomically after upload while stubs, stale revisions, malformed values, and failures preserve the checked built-in presentation.

CommonPlayerSpawnInfo retains the DimensionType holder id for both Login and Respawn; level creation resolves that id through the current synchronized server order before applying identity and every implemented client projection, with a two-entry custom order proving both packet paths. Persistent DimensionType codec semantics remain tracked by their separate holder call.

The synchronized DamageType holder keeps current server order across DamageEvent and component values. DamageEvent stores the resolved resource identity, strictly projects all five DIRECT_CODEC fields when supplied, derives known-pack effects from the generated bootstrap catalog, and routes the six vanilla player hurt-sound choices through native audio; a two-entry custom order and a runtime command test cover the consumer boundary. Persistent DamageType codec and holder-set semantics remain tracked by their separate calls.

Vanilla owns map-decoration types in the immutable client built-in registry. MapItemData retains the holder id, the generated 35-entry order supplies the sprite and item-frame visibility fields consumed by MapDecoration, and both first-person and item-frame surfaces render those values. A focused configuration injection proves that registry data cannot remap the built-in order. The separate persistent holderByName codec remains tracked by its own call.

The metadata holder resolves through synchronized server order and retains exact resource/source/revision identity; both AssetInfo compounds project all wild/tame/angry adult and baby ResourceTextures, all six resources are uploaded, and entity rendering selects the ready age/state texture with vanilla tame-over-angry priority while stubs, stale revisions, malformed values, and failed uploads preserve the checked built-in presentation.

Vanilla 26.1 owns items in the immutable client built-in registry. Every direct Item.STREAM_CODEC network owner implemented by bbb validates the holder against the generated 1506-entry order; ItemStackTemplate additionally rejects air, while the serverbound HashedStack encoder rejects identities outside that same order. World lookup and all numeric consumers share the checked static identity, and a reversed configuration injection proves that RegistryData cannot remap it.

Vanilla 26.1 owns mob effects in the immutable 40-entry client built-in registry. Update/Remove, optional beacon encoding, MobEffectInstance, and suspicious-stew entries all validate their holder at the protocol boundary against the generated order. World state preserves the id for entity replacement/removal and downstream movement, lightmap, HUD, tooltip, and item-component consumers; a reversed configuration injection proves RegistryData cannot remap the identity.

Vanilla 26.1 owns attributes in the immutable 35-entry client built-in registry, while RegistryFriendlyByteBuf still resolves UpdateAttributes holders through the connection RegistryAccess. The protocol decoder preserves the wire id; the world resolves it through FrozenRegistryAccess, maps the resource id to the generated catalog, and accepts it only when the generated target EntityType AttributeSupplier contains that attribute. Context-free ItemAttributeModifiers retains strict built-in validation. Custom holder order, unknown resources, entity-id reuse, session reset, and retained publication isolation have focused coverage.

Vanilla 26.1 owns potions in the immutable 46-entry client built-in registry. PotionContents validates its optional holder at the protocol boundary against the generated order, and world lookup preserves checked static identity in both directions. Tooltip, model-predicate, and persistent-input consumers share the generated resource ids and effects; reversed configuration RegistryData cannot remap any identity.

Vanilla 26.1 synchronizes enchantment definitions and holder order during configuration, then uses Enchantment.STREAM_CODEC only inside the enchantments/stored-enchantments component map. The protocol rejects impossible negative references while retaining nonnegative server ids; world and native consumers resolve custom reordered definitions, tooltip text, attribute effects, item-model predicates, all six value-effect variants, and living-owner crossbow/trident effects through the current session order. A source-derived exhaustive partition guard keeps conditional value/entity/location execution, equipment-drop prevention, and crossbow charging sounds server-owned.

The provides_banner_patterns component retains either its bounded explicit current-session holder ids or one named tag from the exact HolderSet stream shape. Persistent debug reconstruction resolves explicit ids through the current session (fixed catalog only when no synchronized registry exists), preserves named tags, rejects unknown ids, and never expands or substitutes a tag by bootstrap ordinal.

All ten network HolderSet factories retain the exact named-tag or bounded direct-holder wire shape. Fixed item, mob-effect, and entity-type ids are rejected at protocol decode; block and all named sets resolve through generated/frozen registry identity; synchronized damage-type direct sets use server order. Recipe packets validate every Ingredient atomically before replacing state, persistent component reconstruction fails closed without the required tag revision, UpdateTags replacement invalidates removed names, and reverse-order custom damage holders cannot alias bootstrap ordinals. Ingredient's optional empty direct set has no 26.1 clientbound packet consumer in bbb; every present Ingredient decoded by the two clientbound recipe paths uses Vanilla's nonempty CONTENTS_STREAM_CODEC constraints.

Vanilla TagSlotDisplay.STREAM_CODEC sends one item TagKey through recipe display packets and resolves it against the current item registry lookup. Protocol retains the normalized tag identity. The world-owned UpdateRecipes resolver reads ordered members from the current UpdateTags revision for live recipe buttons and tooltips; GhostSlots resolves the packet display once during fillGhostRecipe and retains that ordered ItemStack list while it cycles. Replacement changes live Stonecutter candidates but cannot mutate an already-filled ghost snapshot, removal yields no new candidate, and no path substitutes a bootstrap item ordinal.

The HolderSetCodec call is generic persistent-codec delegation; the five concrete non-DimensionType calls belong to geode, root-system, vegetation-patch, and structure-template worldgen inputs. None of those enclosing codecs is serialized by RegistryDataLoader.SYNCHRONIZED_REGISTRIES, so bbb has no client consumer for these hashed TagKey call sites. DimensionType's synchronized infiniburn field is split into its complete family.

DimensionType.NETWORK_CODEC now validates every required scalar and monster-light provider in the atomic typed registry candidate, normalizes and retains the exact infiniburn TagKey identity, and projects the selected current-session holder into active level diagnostics. Custom reversed block-tag members resolve through the same frozen registry revision, while malformed hashed tags or providers reject the candidate without replacing the prior generation.

Dialog persistent named references resolve through the frozen current-session registry and require synchronized payload data, while inline compounds remain direct values; unknown, stub, malformed, and recursive reference paths stay explicit and bounded.

Persistent trim holder codecs now reconstruct named holders from the current-session resource id and inline holders from their normalized asset fields plus the exact retained Component NBT. ArmorTrim supports named/direct mixtures, provides_trim_material uses the same material encoder, missing Component trees fail closed, and synchronized holder reorder is preserved.

Persistent banner-pattern layers reconstruct named holders from the current-session resource id and inline holders from their validated asset_id/translation_key pair, preserve layer order and dye names, and fail the component closed for unknown session ids or malformed direct identifiers. The fixed vanilla identity catalog is used only when no synchronized registry exists.

The frozen registry boundary distinguishes named resource identities from borrowed inline values. Nested synchronized test environments resolve recursively in session order; the shared SoundEvent codec validates fixed named identities and lenient direct values across registry and dialog consumers; Instrument persistent values preserve named/direct shape. Unknown named sounds reject synchronized candidates atomically.

These factories are generic HolderSet delegation or server-side level generation, trial-spawner persistence, and loot loading paths. Client registry synchronization uses the separate element codecs for Biome and DimensionType and does not send these persistent holder factories; bbb does not own server world generation or loot execution.

PaintingVariant.CODEC is RegistryFixedCodec, so persistent values are named references only: native encodes a synchronized holder through its current-session resource id, uses the fixed vanilla identity only when no synchronized registry exists, and fails closed for direct network holders or unknown session ids rather than inventing a persistent inline compound.

Every client-consumed WorldClock.CODEC reference inside synchronized timeline, dimension-type, and game-test environment payloads resolves by resource identity through the frozen session order. Unknown clocks remain explicit errors, and SetTime continues to use the separately covered network holder path.

TestEnvironmentDefinition timeline lists resolve each Timeline.CODEC name through the frozen synchronized session rather than bootstrap order. The referenced timeline registry has its own typed NETWORK_CODEC projection, and missing identities fail with field-local diagnostics.

These 25 client-observable factories preserve exactly one named resource identity. Persistent component and entity-variant reconstruction resolves synchronized holder ids through the current session and uses generated fixed catalogs only when no server contents exist; dialog and synchronized registry payloads use the shared string-only resolver, and enchantment DamageType/GameEvent references reject missing or malformed candidates atomically.

These 13 factories are generic codec delegation or server-owned advancement, entity-save, POI, beacon-save, chunk-disk, structure-placement, and loot inputs. Their persistent Holder values are not sent as client registry payloads; applicable network projections use separately inventoried holder-id codecs, so bbb has no client consumer for these call sites.

Two rows are generic RegistryCodecs factory delegation and the concrete Ingredient row is the persistent recipe/datapack CODEC. Vanilla client recipe packets use Ingredient.CONTENTS_STREAM_CODEC instead; bbb decodes that separately inventoried network HolderSet shape with nonempty item validation. No persistent custom HolderSet call here is a client wire consumer.

Dialog homogeneous holder sets preserve direct-reference versus direct-inline homogeneity, resolve named tags and resource references through one frozen session revision, retain tag order, and reject mixed, missing, stub, or malformed entries without falling back to bootstrap order.

These five homogeneous-list codecs are worldgen inputs for biome lists, configured carvers/features, and placed features. Vanilla synchronizes each Biome value with Biome.NETWORK_CODEC rather than Biome.LIST_CODEC, and the remaining registries are not synchronized client registries. Their persistent named-or-inline HolderSet forms therefore have no bbb client consumer; synchronized Dialog holder sets remain a separate complete family.

Persistent provides_banner_patterns reconstruction keeps an explicit homogeneous named-holder list in current-session order or the original named tag form. Unknown session ids fail closed, empty explicit sets remain explicit empty lists, tags are not eagerly expanded, and no synchronized registry identity is replaced with a vanilla ordinal.

DimensionType timelines preserve an explicit named holder, ordered named list, or tag-backed set through the frozen timeline registry. Tags retain session order, every referenced identity is checked, layer order reaches timeline sampling, and missing members remain diagnostic instead of falling back by bootstrap ordinal.

The 14 client component and predicate rows decode the exact scalar/list/#tag persistent shape through one frozen RegistryAccess, preserving direct order and named identity while rejecting malformed or missing members. Registry-aware native item-component reconstruction and component-select case remapping use the same session holder and tag boundaries and never substitute bootstrap ordinals; every level-backed item render family supplies the effective stack and current frozen owner.

All six HolderSets inside synchronized Enchantment.DIRECT_CODEC data are checked against the candidate registry revision. Top-level supported, primary, and exclusive identities retain direct-versus-tag form and resolve live tags on query; apply_mob_effect, explode, and summon_entity nested identities are recursively validated before the candidate commits, so failure is atomic.

These 28 factories are server datapack and runtime inputs for advancement predicates, variant selection, enchantment providers, villager trades, world generation, and loot. RegistrySynchronization sends only RegistryDataLoader.SYNCHRONIZED_REGISTRIES; none of these enclosing codecs is a synchronized client registry value, and variant presentation codecs send the selected result rather than the server spawn-condition HolderSet.

These persistent TagKey codecs belong to server advancement predicates, static block bootstrap constructors, recipe/datapack SlotDisplay input, worldgen block predicates and processors, and loot functions/entries. RegistrySynchronization does not serialize those enclosing codecs; recipe displays reach the client through SlotDisplay.STREAM_CODEC, whose network tag is covered separately. bbb therefore has no client consumer for these eleven persistent call sites.
